sections.title: Requirement of Written Tenancy Agreement
sections.description: No person shall, after the commencement of this Act, let or take on rent any premises except by an agreement in writing, which shall be informed to the Rent Authority by the landlord and the tenant jointly.

sections.title: Submission of Tenancy Agreement
sections.description: Every tenancy agreement shall be submitted to the Rent Authority within two months of the execution of the agreement. The Rent Authority shall within a period of sixty days from the date of receipt of such application, make an entry in the register maintained under this Act.

sections.title: Security Deposit
sections.description: No landlord shall claim or receive an amount exceeding two months' rent as security deposit in case of residential premises. In case of non-residential premises, security deposit shall not exceed six months' rent.

sections.title: Revision of Rent
sections.description: Rent shall be revised in accordance with the terms and conditions of the tenancy agreement. In absence of any specific clause, the landlord may increase rent after giving three months' notice.

sections.title: Notice Period for Vacating
sections.description: For residential tenancy, the notice period shall be one month. For non-residential tenancy, the notice period shall be three months. Either party shall give notice before termination of tenancy.

sections.title: Eviction of Tenant
sections.description: A landlord may file an application to the Rent Court for eviction of tenant on grounds including: non-payment of rent for two months or more, subletting without consent, causing damage to premises, landlord's bona fide requirement for personal use.

sections.title: Recovery of Possession by Landlord
sections.description: If a tenant fails to vacate the premises after the expiry of the tenancy period, the landlord may apply to the Rent Court for eviction. The Rent Court shall pass an order within 60 days.

sections.title: Tenant's Rights During Tenancy
sections.description: A tenant shall have the right to peaceful enjoyment of the premises. The landlord shall not interfere with essential services such as water, electricity, sanitation. Landlord must give 24-hour notice before entering premises.

sections.title: Landlord's Obligations
sections.description: The landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs of the premises. The landlord shall ensure all essential services including water, electricity and sanitation are available to the tenant.

sections.title: Tenant's Obligations
sections.description: The tenant shall pay rent on time, maintain the premises in good condition, not cause damage beyond normal wear and tear, not make structural changes without landlord's consent, not sublet without written permission.

sections.title: Subletting
sections.description: No tenant shall sublet the whole or any part of the premises without prior written consent of the landlord. Unauthorized subletting is grounds for eviction.

sections.title: Rent Court
sections.description: Each district shall have a Rent Court to adjudicate disputes between landlords and tenants. The Rent Court shall have the power to grant eviction orders, direct return of security deposit, award compensation.

sections.title: Rent Authority
sections.description: State Government shall designate a Rent Authority for registration of tenancy agreements and maintenance of records. All new tenancy agreements must be filed with the Rent Authority.

sections.title: Appeal
sections.description: Any party aggrieved by an order of the Rent Court may appeal to the Rent Tribunal within a period of 30 days from the date of the order.

Karnataka.applicability: Applicable to premises in urban areas of Karnataka
Karnataka.security_deposit: Maximum 10 months rent in Bengaluru; 3 months in other cities
Karnataka.notice_period: 3 months notice required for eviction in Bengaluru
Karnataka.rent_increase: Not more than 10% increase per annum allowed
Karnataka.registration: Mandatory registration with BBMP/Municipal authorities for Bengaluru
key_provisions: Standard rent concept applies
Controller (District Judge) has jurisdiction over disputes
Eviction only allowed on specified grounds
Tenant has right of first refusal on sale

Maharashtra.applicability: Applicable to all residential and commercial premises in Maharashtra
Maharashtra.security_deposit: Maximum 3 months rent as security deposit
Maharashtra.notice_period: 1 month notice for residential; 3 months for commercial
Maharashtra.rent_increase: Annual increase limited to CPI-linked rates
Maharashtra.registration: Leave and License agreement preferred; must be stamped and registered
key_provisions: Leave and License is common form of tenancy in Maharashtra
Notarized agreement has limited validity
Mumbai has separate provisions under Mumbai Rent Act
Stamp duty: 0.25% of total rent plus deposit
Maharashtra.dispute_forum: Small Causes Court (Mumbai); Rent Controller elsewhere

Tamil Nadu.act_name: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017
Tamil Nadu.security_deposit: Maximum 3 months advance rent as deposit
Tamil Nadu.notice_period: 2 months notice period for residential premises
Tamil Nadu.rent_increase: Rent can be increased after 11 months with prior notice
Tamil Nadu.registration: All agreements must be registered with Rent Authority under 2017 Act
key_provisions: Comprehensive rights and obligations framework
Online registration portal available
Mandatory mediation before court proceedings
Dispute resolution within 60 days

Delhi.act_name: Delhi Rent Act 1958 / Delhi Rent Control Act 1958
Delhi.applicability: Premises with rent below Rs. 3500/month (standard) or all premises (new)
Delhi.rent_increase: 10% per year increase allowed after written notice
Delhi.registration: Rent agreement must be notarized and registered for 12+ months
key_provisions: Old Act covers premises with rent below threshold
Model Tenancy Act being adopted for new tenancies
Rent Controller has jurisdiction for disputes
Strong tenant protection under old Act

Telangana.act_name: Telangana State Apartments (Promotion of Construction and Ownership) Act
Telangana.applicability: Apartments and residential complexes in Telangana
Telangana.security_deposit: Typically 2-10 months rent depending on property
Telangana.rent_increase: As per agreement, typically 5-10% annual increase
Telangana.registration: Agreements must be registered under Registration Act
key_provisions: TSRERA governs real estate projects
Hyderabad Metro Development Authority rules apply
GHMC (HMDA) approval required for construction
Apartment associations have regulatory role
